chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from a man from our companions, said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who buys plaster (gypsum), measures some of it, and takes the remainder without measuring. He said: 'Either take all of it based on his word, or measure all of it.'

key_terms.الْجِصَّ: Plaster or gypsum, a common bulk building material
key_terms.الْغَرَرِ: Uncertainty or ambiguity in a contract

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying bulk goods by measuring only part of them?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the application of *gharar* (uncertainty) in bulk commodity trades by offering two valid methods to ensure fairness: either accepting the seller's estimate for the entire lot or physically measuring the whole quantity. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on eliminating ambiguity in contracts to prevent dispute, a principle deeply rooted in the Prophetic tradition of commercial justice. The ruling underscores the necessity of transparency in transactions involving unmeasured goods, aligning with the broader Islamic legal objective of protecting parties from hidden defects or short-changing.
